corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'High performance and consistently the lowest Wasm footprint in the Rust ecosystem' (no number). Suite data, like-for-like non-keyed (derived from page data, unweighted geometric mean of the medians of the total duration over the 9 CPU benchmarks in results.ts): 0.967x the time of inferno-v8.2.2-non-keyed, 0.905x of svelte-classic-v5.13.0-non-keyed, 1.033x of vanillajs-non-keyed (slower than hand-written JS); rank 8 of 67 non-keyed entries. Cross-mode against keyed React 19.2 hooks (the suite has no non-keyed React entry, and keyed vs non-keyed results are kept in separate tables by the suite): 0.534x React's time (about 1.87x faster, derived from page data); swap 1,000 rows 7.9 ms vs 89.7 ms; create 1,000 rows 22.3 ms vs 23.6 ms; create 10,000 rows 240.1 ms vs 401.0 ms; replace all rows 9.5 ms vs 30.2 ms (non-keyed DOM reuse); remove row 15.9 ms vs 11.3 ms (slower).
corrections.caveats: The headline 1.87x over React is a cross-mode comparison: Kobold is a NON-KEYED implementation (reuses DOM nodes) measured against keyed React 19.2 hooks; the suite keeps keyed and non-keyed results in separate tables and has no non-keyed React entry. Non-keyed DOM reuse explains the 0.31x replace-all-rows ratio; remove-one-row is 1.41x slower than React. Like-for-like, Kobold is only 0.967x Inferno non-keyed's time and 1.033x vanillajs-non-keyed's time (derived from page data), i.e. not faster than hand-written JavaScript. Independent public suite but the CPU model and Chrome flags for the Chrome 154 snapshot are not stated (releases.json labels Chrome 144-146 'macOS' and gives no note for 148-154; the README says the runner was switched to /snap/bin/chromium on Linux in July 2026), so tier B not A. The Wasm bundle is checked in prebuilt ('build-prod is a no-op, the generated javascript is already provided'); it was last rebuilt on 2023-05-26 ('Update kobold to 0.9.1', 'Built'), which is the latest crates.io release, but the repo's master has commits after it (to 2024-05-05). The suite's build-prod-force script calls 'dep:rs' while the script is named 'deps:rs', so the documented rebuild-from-source path is broken. Carries suite note #1139 (does not pass strict CSP). Ratios are the verifier's own unweighted geometric means from the raw results.ts, not the site's weighted score. Repo has not had a commit since 2024-05-05 (stale).

notes: All numbers in the record reproduce exactly from results.ts (medians and geometric means recomputed). Downgraded for an overstated headline: the 1.87x-over-React ratio pits non-keyed Kobold against keyed React, a comparison the suite itself does not make; like-for-like it is about 3% faster than Inferno non-keyed and 3% slower than vanilla JS non-keyed. Tier stays B; metadata (MPL-2.0, 399 stars, last commit 2024-05-05, stale, not a fork) confirmed.
